entries.name: Joseph E. Mulligan

expected.charges: Destruction of government property, mutilation of records, interfering with the Selective Service System, and conspiracy (the May 25, 1969 Chicago draft-record burning).

updates.sentence: Sentenced in 1970 to five years in prison followed by five years of probation for the Chicago 15 draft-record protest. Served two years at Sandstone federal prison, 1970-1972, and was released on parole in 1972. The prison admission and release months and days remain unresolved. The May 25, 1969 arrest and initial Cook County Jail detention are distinct from the later prison term; the intervening period is not treated as continuous custody.

entries.rationale: Participant interview establishes May 25 arrest, 1972 parole and two years served. George Anderson, Jesuits in Jail (1995), printed page 1/PDF page 15, explicitly dates Sandstone imprisonment 1970-1972. Year precision retained; no continuous custody inferred from the 1969 arrest.
